title: Intention: who is this for?
hook: Same prayer, same post, same favor. What makes it count is who you're doing it for.

screens.text: Yesterday was about doing things *well*. Today is about doing them for the *right reason*. It's quieter than it sounds, and it changes everything you do, from prayer to the dishes.
The Prophet ﷺ taught that actions are judged by their intentions, and each person gets what they intended [Bukhari 1]. Your **niyyah** (intention) is simply the "why" in your heart.
bubbles: You don't have to say it out loud.
The good news: with the right niyyah, ordinary things become worship. Going to work to feed your family, sleeping so you can wake for prayer, studying to help people.

screens.after: and each person gets what they intended [Bukhari 1].

options.feedback: Yes. The "why" in your heart is what makes a deed count.
Not quite. Allah judges by intention [Bukhari 1]. Even a good deed you meant but couldn't do is recorded.
Not quite. A small deed with a sincere intention counts. It's the intention [Bukhari 1].

cards.back: For vanity only? It's just a workout. To stay healthy and strong for your family and your prayer? Now it's also worship.

cards.front: Posting your first iftar on social media
cards.back: To share joy or encourage a friend? Good. To collect compliments on how religious you are? That's the thing to watch.

cards.front: Helping set up chairs at the masjid
cards.back: Done for Allah, it's rewarded whether anyone notices or not. Done to be noticed, the reward is the noticing.

cards.front: Meaning to give charity, then the money runs out
cards.back: Allah records a good deed you sincerely meant to do, even if you couldn't do it [Bukhari 6491].

screens.text: **Ikhlas** (sincerity) means doing it for Allah. Its opposite is **riya'** (showing off): doing worship so people will admire you.
bubbles: Allah doesn't look at your looks or your bank balance. He looks at your heart and your deeds [Muslim 2564].
And a deed done for someone else's applause is left to that someone [Muslim 2985].
Scholars count showing off in worship among the worst faults of the heart [Being Muslim, Spiritual Refinement].

screens.situation: Jordan has started reading Qur'an at the masjid after Maghrib. Last week someone said, "Masha Allah, you're so dedicated!" It felt good. Now Jordan worries: "Was that showing off? Maybe I should stop reading there."

options.text: Keep reading there, and quietly renew the intention: "This is for You, Allah"
options.feedback: Yes. Fix the intention, keep the deed. Quitting good deeds out of fear of showing off is a trap.

options.text: Stop reading at the masjid so nobody sees
options.feedback: Not quite. Scholars warn this is a trick: you lose the good deed and the intention isn't fixed either.

options.text: Read louder, so more people are inspired
options.feedback: Not quite. Inspiring others is fine, but if the goal becomes the audience, the heart has drifted.

screens.text: **Don't quit the good deed.** Noticing a show-off feeling is normal. Scholars teach: keep doing the deed and steer the intention back to Allah [Being Muslim, Spiritual Refinement].
bubbles: Feeling happy when someone says something kind isn't showing off by itself. The question is what you were doing it *for*.
Intention isn't a one-time switch. You check it, and you correct it, for life.

screens.prompt: Hannah realizes halfway through helping at a food drive that she mostly came for the photos. What's the best move?

options.text: Keep helping, and turn her intention back to Allah right now
options.feedback: Right. Intentions can be corrected mid-deed. The work is still good.

options.text: Leave, since the deed is ruined anyway
options.feedback: Not quite. Nothing is ruined while she can still fix her intention. Leaving loses the good she's doing.

options.text: Post the photos to prove she's sincere
options.feedback: Not quite. Proving sincerity to people is still about the people.

screens.title: A quick check before you post about your faith

steps.text: Ask: would I still do this deed if nobody ever saw it?
Ask: does sharing it help someone, or just help my image?

screens.done_text: Sharing isn't wrong. Many converts find each other by posting. The check just keeps your heart honest.

screens.prompt: Pick one thing you do every day (work, school, cooking, caring for someone). What intention could turn it into worship? Write it in one sentence.

chips: Do I have to say my intention out loud before praying?
Is it showing off to post about my shahada?
How do I know if my intention is sincere?
I feel fake when people praise me at the masjid. What do I do?

steps: Before your next prayer, pause for one breath
Tell Allah in your heart who it's for
Do one good deed today that nobody will ever know about
screens.optional_extra: Look at your last few posts about your faith. Run the three-question check on them. No need to delete anything; just notice.

screens.text: Actions count by their intention. Do it for Allah, check your "why" often, and never drop a good deed out of fear of showing off.
Nobody's heart is pure all the time. Just keep turning it back.

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- Actions are judged by intentions, and each person gets what they intended [Bukhari 1].
- Allah looks at hearts and deeds, not appearances or wealth [Muslim 2564].
- A deed done to be seen by others, in Allah's words, is left to the one it was done for [Muslim 2985]. Scholars treat showing off in worship (riya') as a serious fault of the heart [Being Muslim, Spiritual Refinement].
- A sincerely intended good deed that the person couldn't do is still recorded as a good deed [Bukhari 6491].
- Scholars teach not to abandon a good deed for fear of showing off, but to keep it and correct the intention [Being Muslim, Spiritual Refinement].
- With a good intention, everyday actions (work, sleep, study, caring for family) can be acts of worship [Revealed Path ch. 15, ch. 24].

**Likely questions**
- *"Do I say my intention out loud?"* No. The intention is in the heart: knowing which prayer you're about to pray is enough. Some people say it quietly to help focus; it isn't required. Don't make it a source of worry (link Day 26 on waswasa).
- *"Is it showing off to post about my shahada?"* Not necessarily. Sharing good news, encouraging others or finding community is fine. Suggest the three-question check. Also remind them privacy is their choice; they don't owe anyone a post.
- *"How do I know if I'm sincere?"* Nobody is sure all the time, and worrying about it is itself a sign of care. Keep renewing it; do some good deeds privately.
- *"People praise me and I feel fake."* Normal. Thank them, make du'a, keep going, and keep some deeds secret.

**Escalate:** persistent, distressing doubts that none of their worship counts (possible waswasa): offer the mentor or imam.

**Don't**
- Don't make the convert anxious about every motive. The point is a gentle habit of checking, not scrupulosity.
- Don't tell anyone to stop a good deed because their intention may be mixed.
- Don't judge other people's intentions; only Allah knows hearts.

- [Bukhari 6491](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6491): an intended good deed is recorded.
- [Muslim 2564](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2564): Allah looks at hearts and deeds, not bodies and faces.
- [Muslim 2985](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2985): Allah needs no partner; a deed done for another is left to that partner.
- Being Muslim a Practical Guide, Spiritual Refinement (intention, showing off, not abandoning deeds).
- The Revealed Path Part III, ch. 15 (heart and limbs); ch. 24 (earning with the right intention as worship).
